'''Elizabeth Alison Thompson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born May 22, 1949) is a British-born American [[statistician]] at the [[University of Washington]].{{r|cv}} Her research concerns the use of genetic data to infer relationships between individuals and populations.{{r|2uwnas}} She was the 2017–2018 president of the [[International Biometric Society]].{{r|ibsgov}}

==Education and career==
Thompson studied at [[Newnham College, Cambridge]], earning [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|first-class honours]] in the [[mathematical tripos]] in 1970 and completing a diploma in mathematical statistics in 1971.{{r|cv}} She continued at Cambridge for graduate studies, earning a Ph.D. in statistics in 1974 under the supervision of [[A. W. F. Edwards]].{{r|cv|mgp}}

After postdoctoral studies at [[Stanford University]] she returned to Cambridge as a lecturer in mathematics and mathematical statistics and fellow of [[King's College, Cambridge]]. She became a fellow of Newnham in 1981. She moved to the Department of Statistics at the [[University of Washington]] in 1985, and added a joint appointment to the Department of Biostatistics in 1988. She became a U.S. citizen in 1997.{{r|cv}}

==Awards and honors==
Thompson was awarded the degree of Doctor of Science (ScD) by Cambridge University in 1988 based on her published work,{{r|cv}} and became an honorary fellow of Newnham in 2013.{{r|cv|hfn}}

She became a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1998.{{r|cv}}
In 2008 she joined the [[National Academy of Sciences]].{{r|cv|2uwnas}} She was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2023.{{r|frs}}

She is the [[Carnegie Centenary Professor]] for 2017 at the [[University of St Andrews]].{{r|ccp}}
